hero.lead: Give your AI agent a real BOL inbox. Read, search, send, reply, schedule and organize mail over IMAP with your ordinary BOL password and the settings verified on this page.
hero.answer: Claude cannot reach BOL Mail on its own. MCPEmails is a hosted MCP server that connects it over IMAP at imap.bol.com.br on port 993, authenticating with your BOL password, so Claude, Cursor or any MCP client can read, search, send and organize that mail. BOL is operated by UOL on the same mail platform, and the settings look close enough to UOL's to copy, which is where most mistakes come from: BOL's outgoing server takes implicit TLS on port 465 while UOL's takes STARTTLS on 587. There is no app password and nothing to generate. One inbox on MCPEmails is free.
hero.meta1: Your BOL password, no app password

method.title: How BOL Mail connects: IMAP and SMTP on the UOL platform
method.body: BOL serves IMAP at imap.bol.com.br on port 993 over implicit TLS, and submission at smtps.bol.com.br on port 465, also implicit TLS. BOL is operated by UOL, and the server behind both is the same Dovecot installation UOL runs, with the same message size ceiling and the same naming. Authentication is ordinary. There is no app password and no separate authorization code, just your BOL password, with the full address as the username. The one wrinkle is the username form: the Mozilla autoconfiguration entry for bol.com.br, which Thunderbird and other clients use to fill in settings, records the login as the part before the @ rather than the whole address, so if the full address is refused, the shorter form is the next thing to try. The hosts and ports on this page were confirmed from a live TLS connection, and the settings table shows the date.

setup.p: Sign up at mcpemails.com. The free plan connects one inbox and stays free, with no card required. Leave it open; the BOL side takes about a minute.

setup.h: Check that the mailbox opens in the BOL webmail
setup.p: Sign in to the BOL webmail with the address and password you intend to use. If the webmail itself refuses the password, no mail client will accept it either, so reset it there first. A mailbox that opens normally in the webmail is ready to connect.

setup.h: Enter your address and password in MCPEmails
setup.p: Choose IMAP / SMTP and enter the complete address, such as nome@bol.com.br, together with your BOL password. The hosts and ports are prefilled and were confirmed from a live TLS connection. Note the outgoing port: BOL takes implicit TLS on 465, which is not the same as the setting its sibling service uses.

setup.h: Paste the MCP URL into your AI client
setup.p: Drop https://mcpemails.com/api/mcp into Claude, Cursor or ChatGPT, authorize, and your agent can read, search, send, reply, forward, schedule and organize the BOL mailbox.

gotchas.h: The username may be the login without the domain
gotchas.p: Most providers expect the whole address in the username field, and that is the form to try first. The Mozilla autoconfiguration entry for bol.com.br, the one mail clients use to set BOL up automatically, records the username as the local part only, the login without @bol.com.br. If the full address is rejected in exactly the way a bad password would be, switching to the short form is a ten second test worth running before resetting anything. UOL documents the same two forms for its own mailboxes.

gotchas.h: UOL's settings look close enough to copy, and the SMTP port differs
gotchas.p: BOL is run by UOL on the same platform, and the two sets of settings are similar enough that people substitute one for the other. The transport is where that breaks. BOL's submission host takes implicit TLS on port 465. UOL's takes STARTTLS on port 587. Both hosts are named with the same smtps prefix, so the name gives you no warning. Using the wrong combination usually hangs rather than erroring, because a client expecting a TLS handshake on a plaintext port waits for a greeting that never comes.

gotchas.h: No MOVE, no SPECIAL-USE, and folders matched by name
gotchas.p: BOL's IMAP server does not advertise the MOVE extension, so filing a message runs as a copy, a flag update and an expunge instead of one atomic command, and a connection lost midway can leave the message briefly in both folders. It also omits SPECIAL-USE, so folders are matched by name rather than by role. If the mailbox uses Portuguese folder names such as Enviados, Rascunhos or Lixeira, MCPEmails still resolves them, and if your agent files something in the wrong place, name the target folder in the instruction.

limits: BOL itself decides which mailboxes have client access. If a correct password is refused both here and in every other mail program, the restriction is on BOL's side and MCPEmails cannot work around it.
There is no IDLE support, so mail is polled rather than pushed. Your agent sees a new message the next time it checks rather than the moment it arrives.
The SMTP server accepts messages up to about 33 MB. A forward carrying larger attachments is refused at send time rather than queued.

faq.q: Does Claude work with BOL email?
faq.a: Not directly. Claude has no built-in BOL connector and cannot open an IMAP connection by itself, so it needs an MCP server such as MCPEmails in front of the mailbox. That connection is over IMAP at imap.bol.com.br, and gives Claude read, search, send, reply, forward, schedule and organize access. The same connection works from Cursor, ChatGPT and other MCP clients.

faq.q: What are the BOL IMAP and SMTP settings?
faq.a: IMAP is imap.bol.com.br on port 993 with implicit TLS. Outgoing mail is smtps.bol.com.br on port 465, also implicit TLS. Log in with your bol.com.br address and your BOL password. Both hosts were verified from a live TLS connection on the date shown on this page.

faq.q: Why does my BOL password not work in a mail client?
faq.a: First confirm the password opens the BOL webmail; if it does not, reset it there. If it does, try the username without the domain part, since the public autoconfiguration entry for BOL records the login in that shorter form. If both forms are refused in every mail program, the mailbox has no client access on BOL's side, and only BOL can change that.

faq.q: Is BOL the same as UOL?
faq.a: BOL is operated by UOL and runs on the same mail platform, but they are separate services with separate mailboxes, separate hostnames and separate settings. In particular the outgoing port and encryption differ between the two, so copying one configuration onto the other does not work.

faq.q: Does BOL need an app password?
faq.a: No. BOL has no app-specific password scheme and issues no separate authorization code. Your ordinary BOL password authenticates both IMAP and SMTP. That also means changing your BOL password breaks any connected client until you update the stored credential.

faq.q: Is my BOL mail stored on your servers?
faq.a: No. Messages are fetched live from BOL over IMAP for each request and passed to your AI client. Credentials are encrypted at rest, and message bodies are not retained after the request that asked for them.
